answer: Persistent Compute-Hour Ledger. Each identity must accumulate a slow tide of verified compute-hours before gaining full API privileges. Hours come from real work judged by downstream consumers, and the ledger decays over time. An attacker who tries to wander across many fresh identities must run genuine workloads on each one for weeks before any pays off. A separate marble-draw audit randomly replays a fraction of claimed hours; failing burns the whole ledger. Cost per fake identity is sustained compute plus the risk of losing all accumulated hours.
